newsitem.title: UK: Russia issues second international bond.
newsitem.headline: Russia issues second international bond.

text.p: Russia raised 2.0 billion marks ($1.2 billion) on Thursday with the launch of its second-ever international bond issue.

The seven-year bond was priced to yield 3.70 percentage points over German government bonds and paid a nine percent annual coupon. Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell underwrote the deal.
The mark bond followed a successful $1.0 billion five-year debut deal launched by Russia last November, its first foreign bond since the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.
Thursday's deal has opened up another important source of funds for Russia, and will enable other Russian borrowers and former Soviet republics to also tap these investors.
Buyers of high-yielding mark Eurobonds tend to be small German and Benelux investors, in contrast to mainly institutional buyers of Eurobonds denominated in dollars.
The November dollar bond, the largest debut bond ever issued, was heavily oversubscribed and Russia was able to raise two or three times more than it had originally planned.
Similarly, demand for the mark paper proved robust, with Russia expected to launch a one billion mark deal initially.
But the bond launch comes against a background of soft market conditions, bankers said.
Demand for high-yielding bond issues by emerging market countries has weakened due to sharp falls in prices triggered by worries of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
Russia paid a higher premium over government bonds than had been originally expected to reflect the change in the market.
The bond went ahead despite uncertainty about the shape of Russia's government.
President Boris Yeltsin will meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin later to discuss the new line-up of the cabinet following Yeltsin's decision to reshuffle the government dramatically.
Yeltsin blasted the government for failing to tackle the economic and social crisis in Russia in his state of the nation address last Thursday. ($ = 1.695 German Marks)
